```{r load-data, include=FALSE}
# Load your data here

#Loading Data and cleaning
communities_clean <- read.csv("data/communities_heading.data") |> 
  mutate(across(everything() & !c(communityname.string), ~as.numeric(.)),
         LemasGangUnitDeploy.numeric = case_when(
           LemasGangUnitDeploy.numeric == 1 ~ "Yes",
           LemasGangUnitDeploy.numeric == 0 ~ "No",
           LemasGangUnitDeploy.numeric == 0.5 ~ "PrtTime"
         ))

```

```{r Data-split, include = FALSE }
#Split the data into a training and testing subset
set.seed(1234)
communities_split <- initial_split(communities_clean, prop = 0.75)
train <- training(communities_split)
test <- testing(communities_split)

#Define the Model
#We are going to use a regular linear model
communities_mod <- linear_reg() |> 
  set_engine("lm")

#Variable List
Variables <- c("ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric","medIncome.numeric","perCapInc.numeric","PctPopUnderPov.numeric","pctWWage.numeric","pctWFarmSelf.numeric","pctWInvInc.numeric","pctWSocSec.numeric","pctWPubAsst.numeric","pctWRetire.numeric","PctUnemployed.numeric","PctEmploy.numeric","PctEmplManu.numeric","PctEmplProfServ.numeric","PctLess9thGrade.numeric","PctNotHSGrad.numeric","PctBSorMore.numeric","LemasSwFTFieldPerPop.numeric","LemasPctPolicOnPatr.numeric","LemasPctOfficDrugUn.numeric","PolicBudgPerPop.numeric","LemasSwFTPerPop.numeric","LemasGangUnitDeploy.numeric")
```

# Analysing Wealth and Violent Crimes

---

## Wealth Correlated With Violent Crimes

```{r Analyse wealth,out.width="80%",echo=FALSE, fig.align='center'}
#Smaller Data set for this Analysis
communities_W <- communities_clean |> 
  select(medIncome.numeric,perCapInc.numeric,PctPopUnderPov.numeric,ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric)

#Correlation Heat Map plot
communities_W |> 
  summarise(mutate(
    across(!c(ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric), ~ cor(ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric,.))
  )) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) |> 
ggplot(aes(x="ViolentCrime",y=reorder(Variable,Value), fill = Value))+
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(Value, 2)), size = 4) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "steelblue",
    mid = "white",
    high = "coral",
    midpoint = 0,
    limits = c(-1, 1)
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Wealth & Crime Correlation",
    x = "",
    y = "",
    fill = "Correlation (r)"
  )


```
]

---

## Modeling Violent Crimes based on Wealth

```{r Model W, include=FALSE}

#Select the necessary columns from the training and test data
training_data <- train |>
  select(ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric,medIncome.numeric,perCapInc.numeric,PctPopUnderPov.numeric)
testing_data <- test |>
    select(ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric,medIncome.numeric,perCapInc.numeric,PctPopUnderPov.numeric)

folds <- vfold_cv(training_data, v = 10)

#Make the recipe for the Models
recipe <- recipe(ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric ~ ., data = training_data) |> 
  step_naomit() |> 
  step_dummy(all_nominal(), -all_outcomes()) |> 
  step_zv(all_predictors())

#Finalise the Workflow
communities_wflow <- workflow() |> 
  add_model(communities_mod) |> 
  add_recipe(recipe)

#Train the Model with the Variables
Fit <- communities_wflow |> 
  fit(training_data)

RMSE_RSQ <- communities_wflow |> 
  fit_resamples(folds) |> 
  collect_metrics(summarize = FALSE) |> 
  select(id,.estimate,.metric) |> 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = .metric,
    values_from = .estimate
  )

RSqrd_Test <- rsq(Predict, truth = ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric, .pred)

#Test the model
Predict <- predict(Fit, testing_data) |> 
  bind_cols(testing_data |> select(ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric)) |> 
  mutate(
    resid = ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric - .pred
  )

#Look at residuals vs predicted value
Predict |> 
ggplot(
  aes(x = .pred,
      y = resid,
      colour = ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric)
)+
  geom_point()

#Store some data for later comparison
StatTable_W <- tibble(Model = c("Model Wealth"),
                   CV_RSqrd_Train = round(mean(RMSE_RSQ$rsq), digits = 3),
                   RSqrd_Test = round(RSqrd_Test$.estimate, digits = 3),
                   AdjRSqrd_Train = round(c(glance(Fit)$adj.r.squared), digits = 3),
                   CV_RMSE = mean(RMSE_RSQ$rmse),
                   NumOfPred = c(nrow(summary(recipe))-1))



```

```{r Cor-vs-Eq W, echo = false}
COR <- communities_W |> 
  summarise(mutate(
    across(!c(ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric), ~ cor(ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric,.))
  )) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Cor"
  )

Equation <- tidy(Fit) |> 
  select(estimate, term) |>
  filter_out(term == "(Intercept)") |> 
  rename(Variable = "term",
         'Eq. Const.' = "estimate")

CorEq_Tbl <- full_join(COR, Equation) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c("Eq. Const.",Cor),
    names_to = "Type",
    values_to = "Value"
  )

ordering <- CorEq_Tbl |> 
  filter(Type == "Cor") |> 
  arrange((Value)) |> 
  pull(Variable) |> 
  as.factor()

CorEq_Tbl$Variable <- factor(CorEq_Tbl$Variable, levels = ordering)

CorEq_Tbl |> 
ggplot(aes(x=Type,y = Variable, fill = Value))+
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(Value, 3)), size = 4) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "steelblue",
    mid = "white",
    high = "coral",
    midpoint = 0,
    limits = c(-1, 1)
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation Vs Equation Value",
    x = "",
    y = "",
    fill = "Value (r)"
  )


```

```{r Police Data, echo=FALSE, fig.align='center'}
    across(!c(ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric), ~ cor(ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric,.))
  )) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x="ViolentCrime",y=reorder(Variable,Value), fill = Value))+
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(Value, 2)), size = 4) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "steelblue",
    mid = "white",
    high = "coral",
    midpoint = 0,
    limits = c(-1, 1)
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Occupation Correlated with Violent Crime",
    x = "",
    y = "",
    fill = "Correlation (r)"
  )

```

```{r Model P, include=FALSE}

#Select the necessary columns fomr the training and test data
training_data <- train |>
select(ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric,LemasSwFTFieldPerPop.numeric,LemasPctPolicOnPatr.numeric,LemasPctOfficDrugUn.numeric,PolicBudgPerPop.numeric,LemasSwFTPerPop.numeric,LemasGangUnitDeploy.numeric) |> 
  drop_na()
testing_data <- test |>
select(ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric,LemasSwFTFieldPerPop.numeric,LemasPctPolicOnPatr.numeric,LemasPctOfficDrugUn.numeric,PolicBudgPerPop.numeric,LemasSwFTPerPop.numeric,LemasGangUnitDeploy.numeric) |> 
  drop_na()

folds <- vfold_cv(training_data, v = 10)

#Make the recipe for the Models
recipe <- recipe(ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric ~ ., data = training_data) |> 
  step_naomit() |> 
  step_dummy(all_nominal(), -all_outcomes()) |> 
  step_zv(all_predictors())

#Finalise the Workflow
communities_wflow <- workflow() |> 
  add_model(communities_mod) |> 
  add_recipe(recipe)

#Train the Model with the Variables
Fit <- communities_wflow |> 
  fit(data = training_data)

RMSE_RSQ <- communities_wflow |> 
  fit_resamples(folds) |> 
  collect_metrics(summarize = FALSE) |> 
  select(id,.estimate,.metric) |> 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = .metric,
    values_from = .estimate
  )

RSqrd_Test <- rsq(Predict, truth = ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric, .pred)

#Test the model
Predict <- predict(Fit, testing_data) |> 
  bind_cols(testing_data |> select(ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric)) |> 
  mutate(
    resid = ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric - .pred
  )

#Look at residuals vs predicted value
Predict |> 
ggplot(
  aes(x = .pred,
      y = resid,
      colour = ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric)
)+
  geom_point()

#Store some data for later comparison
StatTable_P <- tibble(Model = c("Model Police"),
                   CV_RSqrd_Train = round(mean(RMSE_RSQ$rsq), digits = 3),
                   RSqrd_Test = round(RSqrd_Test$.estimate, digits = 3),
                   AdjRSqrd_Train = round(c(glance(Fit)$adj.r.squared), digits = 3),
                   CV_RMSE = mean(RMSE_RSQ$rmse),
                   NumOfPred = c(nrow(summary(recipe))-1))
```

```{r Cor-vs-Eq P, echo=FALSE}
#Correlation Values
COR <- communities_P |> 
  summarise(mutate(
    across(!c(ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric), ~ cor(ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric,.))
  )) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Cor"
  )

Equation <- tidy(Fit) |> 
  select(estimate, term) |>
  filter_out(term == "(Intercept)") |> 
  rename(Variable = "term",
         'Eq. Const.' = "estimate")

CorEq_Tbl <- full_join(COR, Equation) |> 
  drop_na() |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c("Eq. Const.",Cor),
    names_to = "Type",
    values_to = "Value"
  )

ordering <- CorEq_Tbl |> 
  filter(Type == "Cor") |> 
  arrange((Value)) |> 
  pull(Variable) |> 
  as.factor()

CorEq_Tbl$Variable <- factor(CorEq_Tbl$Variable, levels = ordering)

CorEq_Tbl |> 
ggplot(aes(x=Type,y = Variable, fill = Value))+
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(Value, 3)), size = 4) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "steelblue",
    mid = "white",
    high = "coral",
    midpoint = 0,
    limits = c(-1, 1)
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation Vs Equation Value",
    x = "",
    y = "",
    fill = "Value (r)"
  )
```

```{r Model All Backward-Analysis, include=FALSE}
training_data <- train |>
select(Variables) |> 
  drop_na()
testing_data <- test |>
select(Variables) |> 
  drop_na()

#Make the recipe for the Models
recipe <- recipe(ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric ~ ., data = training_data) |> 
  step_naomit() |> 
  step_dummy(all_nominal(), -all_outcomes()) |> 
  step_zv(all_predictors())

folds <- vfold_cv(training_data, v = 5)

#Variables for the Repeat function
vars <- Variables[!Variables %in% c("ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric")]
dropped <- character(0)
best <- cv_rmse(dropped)
history <- tibble()

repeat {
  remaining <- setdiff(vars, added)
  if (length(remaining) == 0) break
  scores <- map_dbl(remaining, ~ cv_rmse(setdiff(vars, c(added, .x))))
  history <- bind_rows(history,
    tibble(round = length(added) + 1, add = remaining, cv_rmse = scores))
  if (min(scores) >= best) break
  added <- c(added, remaining[which.min(scores)])
  best  <- min(scores)
}

print(best)
print(remaining)

#Train the Best Model
Fit <- workflow() |> 
  add_model(communities_mod) |> 
  add_recipe(recipe |> step_rm(starts_with(dropped))) |> 
  fit(training_data)

Equation <- tidy(Fit) |> 
  select(estimate, term) |>
  filter_out(term == "(Intercept)") |> 
  rename(Variable = "term",
         'Eq. Const.' = "estimate")

#Test the model on the testing data
Predict <- predict(Fit, testing_data) |> 
  bind_cols(testing_data |> select(ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric)) |> 
  mutate(
    resid = ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric - .pred
  )

#Look at residuals vs predicted value
Predict |> 
ggplot(
  aes(x = .pred,
      y = resid,
      colour = ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric)
)+
  geom_point()

#Store some data for later comparison
RMSE_RSQ <- communities_wflow |> 
  fit_resamples(folds) |> 
  collect_metrics(summarize = FALSE) |> 
  select(id,.estimate,.metric) |> 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = .metric,
    values_from = .estimate
  )

StatTable_A_BW_RMSE <- tibble(Model = c("Model All FW"),
                   CV_RSqrd_Train = round(mean(RMSE_RSQ$rsq), digits = 3),
                   RSqrd_Test = round(RSqrd_Test$.estimate, digits = 3),
                   AdjRSqrd_Train = round(c(glance(Fit)$adj.r.squared), digits = 3),
                   CV_RMSE = mean(RMSE_RSQ$rmse),
                   NumOfPred = c(nrow(summary(recipe))-1))


```

```{r Model Forward Analysis 1, include=FALSE}
#Select the Variables
training_data <- train |>
select(Variables) |> 
  drop_na()
testing_data <- test |>
select(Variables) |> 
  drop_na()

#Make the recipe for the Models
recipe <- recipe(ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric ~ ., data = training_data) |> 
  step_naomit() |> 
  step_dummy(all_nominal(), -all_outcomes()) |> 
  step_zv(all_predictors())

folds <- vfold_cv(training_data, v = 5)

#Make the Variables for the repeat function

vars <- Variables[!Variables %in% c("ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric")]
added <- character(0)
best <- Inf
history <- tibble()

#Create the drop CV_RMSE function
cv_rmse <- function(drop){
  workflow() |> 
    add_model(communities_mod) |> 
    add_recipe(recipe |> step_rm(starts_with(drop))) |> 
    fit_resamples(folds) |> 
    collect_metrics() |> 
    filter(.metric == "rmse") |> 
    pull(mean)
}

#Create the repeat function
repeat{
  remaining <- setdiff(vars, added)
  if (length(remaining) == 0) break
  scores <- map_dbl(remaining, ~cv_rmse(setdiff(vars, c(added, .x))))
  history <- bind_rows(history,
                       tibble( round = length(added) + 1, add = remaining, cv_rmse =scores))
  if(min(scores) >= best) break
  added <- c(added, remaining[which.min(scores)])
  best <- min(scores)
}

print(best)
print(remaining)
print(added)

#Use the 'remain' vector to create the new linear model
Fit <- workflow() |> 
  add_model(communities_mod) |> 
  add_recipe(recipe |> step_rm(starts_with(remaining))) |> 
  fit(training_data)

Equation <- tidy(Fit) |> 
  select(estimate, term) |>
  filter_out(term == "(Intercept)") |> 
  rename(Variable = "term",
         'Eq. Const.' = "estimate")

#Test the model on the testing data
Predict <- predict(Fit, testing_data) |> 
  bind_cols(testing_data |> select(ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric)) |> 
  mutate(
    resid = ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric - .pred
  )

#Look at residuals vs predicted value
Predict |> 
ggplot(
  aes(x = .pred,
      y = resid,
      colour = ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric)
)+
  geom_point()

#Store some data for later comparison
RMSE_RSQ <- communities_wflow |> 
  fit_resamples(folds) |> 
  collect_metrics(summarize = FALSE) |> 
  select(id,.estimate,.metric) |> 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = .metric,
    values_from = .estimate
  )

StatTable_A_FW_RMSE <- tibble(Model = c("Model All FW"),
                   CV_RSqrd_Train = round(mean(RMSE_RSQ$rsq), digits = 3),
                   RSqrd_Test = round(RSqrd_Test$.estimate, digits = 3),
                   AdjRSqrd_Train = round(c(glance(Fit)$adj.r.squared), digits = 3),
                   CV_RMSE = mean(RMSE_RSQ$rmse),
                   NumOfPred = c(nrow(summary(recipe))-1))

```

# Math Expressions

You can write LaTeX math expressions inside a pair of dollar signs, e.g. &#36;\alpha+\beta$ renders $\alpha+\beta$. You can use the display style with double dollar signs:

```
$$\bar{X}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^nX_i$$
```

$$\bar{X}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^nX_i$$

Limitations:

1. The source code of a LaTeX math expression must be in one line, unless it is inside a pair of double dollar signs, in which case the starting `$$` must appear in the very beginning of a line, followed immediately by a non-space character, and the ending `$$` must be at the end of a line, led by a non-space character;

1. There should not be spaces after the opening `$` or before the closing `$`.

1. Math does not work on the title slide (see [#61](https://github.com/yihui/xaringan/issues/61) for a workaround).
